_readme: SPELL CATALOG: the single source for every spell's REACH TAG. Edit this file, then run `node tools/gen_spells.js`.
The generator rewrites the GEN:BEGIN/GEN:END spell_range_lookup block in web/mygame/scenes/combat.txt.
Never edit inside a generated block by hand: the next run overwrites it.
WHY: a spell used to be classified (ranged or not) by whatever its call site happened to hard-code, so
adding a cantrip meant remembering which of several sites needed a matching condition. The tag lives here
once and the lookup resolves it from check_skill, the variable every attack option already sets before it
rolls. Adding a spell is then one entry here plus its call site -- it can never be mis-tagged by omission.
The RANGE TAG answers TWO different questions, and the combat engine asks them separately:
can I reach them?    -> gates whether the option is offered at all (close/touch cannot be used at the
wrong tier; they are UNAVAILABLE, not merely penalised)
is the shot spoiled? -> gates disadvantage (ranged ONLY, and only at Engaged)
Collapsing those two is a real bug: a touch spell at Mid-Range should not be offered at disadvantage.
Spell fields:
id      internal id, matching the *_cantrip / *_spell / race_cantrip variable values (snake_case)
name    the display name, which is what check_skill is set to at the call site -- this is the lookup key
range   ranged | close | touch (see below)
RANGE TAGS:
ranged  Can hit any enemy at any tier (0=Engaged .. 3=Long Range). If the target is Engaged, the attack
roll has DISADVANTAGE -- the close-combat ranged penalty, identical for a weapon, a thrown
weapon, or a spell. Melee attacks never take this penalty.
close   Can only hit enemies at Close (1) or Mid-Range (2) -- NOT Engaged. Offered at those tiers, and
never offered at Engaged, so a melee enemy closing on the caster takes the spell away. No
penalty of its own (the target is never adjacent, so the close-combat rule cannot apply).
Reserved for future use; no spell uses it yet.
touch   Can only hit an Engaged enemy (0) -- never offered at any other tier. No penalty: a touch spell
IS a melee attack, and melee attacks are never penalised for being in melee.
Both close and touch are implemented now so the first spell that needs one costs nothing to add.
REACH CLASS (2026-10-12, the user's call): how far the spell reaches, a second field beside the range tag. It is a NAME, so it means the same in the four-band and six-band lanes:
touch   Engaged only (the same as the touch range tag)
short   up to Close (1)
medium  up to Mid-Range (2 in the four-band lane, 3 in the six-band one: combat_reach_medium)
long    any distance (the default for a spell that gives none)

The generator writes the spell_reach_flags block in combat.txt, one spell_reach_ok_<id> flag per spell for the hub to gate its option on, and the reach test inside spell_range_lookup. A spell whose option is not yet wired to its flag is simply not range limited.
